summary: Munkhjavkhlan Baatar worked in philosophy and Indology. He earned a PhD from the National University of Mongolia and subsequently held a post there.

Murray Barnson Emeneau was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, Edgar Sturtevant, and Edward Sapir. He taught at Yale (1926–1939) and UC Berkeley (1940–1971), and visited Aligarh Muslim University.

Murray Fowler worked in linguistics and Indology. After studies at Minnesota, Oregon, Vienna, and Harvard under Joshua Whatmough, he taught at Pomona (1929–1930), Purdue (1931–1936), Harvard (1939–1946), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1946–1953).

Musashi Tachikawa specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya and Harvard under Ingalls and others, later holding posts at Nagoya University (1970), National Museum of Ethnology (~1989–2005), and Aichi Gakuin University (~2005–2012).

Muzaffar Alam works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he taught (~1973–2001) before becoming a professor at the University of Chicago (~2001).

Myles Dillon was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at UCD, Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and Trinity College Dublin, he held professorships at Wisconsin-Madison (1937–1946), Chicago (1946–1947), and Edinburgh (~1946–1947), later directing DIAS (1960–1968).
Myokyo-ni was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Graz and trained under traditional teacher Soko Morinaga in 1984.
Myōsei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1987) and later professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.

Mysore Hiriyanna was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Madras Christian College under Perisamy Tirumalacharya and Kashi Sesharamasastry, he was a Sanskrit professor at Maharaja's College, Mysore and the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas studied at Mysore, Mumbai, and Oxford under Ghurye, Radcliffe-Brown, and Evans-Pritchard. He taught at Baroda (~1951–1959), Delhi (1959), and chaired the Institute for Social and Economic Change (1972–1979).

Mário Bruno Cruz works in Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at NOVA University of Lisbon and studied for a doctorate at the University of Lisbon, working primarily as a translator and reviewer for various publishers and organizations.

Mélanie Vandenhelsken specializes in Tibetology and religious studies, earning a doctorate from the University of Montpellier (1996–2003). She held posts at Montpellier, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, University of Vienna, and Webster Vienna Private University.
Mónika Kiss is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University as a PhD student under Masanori Yamaji, Robert F. Rhodes, and Nozomu Saito.
N. A. Gore was an Indologist who worked as a librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957–1958) and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).

N. A. Jayawickrama was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He held professorships at the University of Ceylon (attested 1974) and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

N. Aiyaswami Sastri worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Madras Sanskrit College and Visva-Bharati University, he held posts at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

N. D. Mironov was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg, Strasbourg, Berlin, and Bonn. He held teaching posts at Moscow State University (1905), Irkutsk State University (1918), and the Asiatic Museum (1913–1918).
N. J. Karthika works in computational fields and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and subsequently held a post there.

N. Lakshminarayana Rao worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and Special Officer (Epigraphy) for the Government of India in 1956.
N. R. Bhatt was an Indologist who held positions at the French Institute of Pondicherry and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 1966).
